trials.proposal_diagnosis: The only allowed root is T0026, whose own root analysis classifies it as a 'trace_based_hypothesis_not_proven_cause' and whose decisive gap is the ABSENCE of a retrieved span naming the diagnosis as an indication for the predicted option. Encoding a procedure that defaults to the option whose label indication section contains the closest matching syndrome would (a) turn the presence/absence of a retrieved indication span into an option preference, which the contract explicitly forbids ('absence of a retrieved span must not eliminate a treatment'; 'never turn the presence of a label span into a preference for that option'), and (b) effectively assert a new medical rule (one macrolide preferred over another) unsupported by the sources, since both candidate macrolides lack an explicit bacillary-angiomatosis indication span. The required single trigger is conditional_question. For a valid card I need at least two observed FAILURES in the triggered region sharing the trace-level cause, and at least two prior SUCCESSES including one inside the region, explained. But among the conditional_question failures, only T0026 has a traced indication-matching root; T0046, T0013, T0017, T0061, T0062 are different question types (resistance/next-step/dose-adequacy/management) with no shared traced indication-selection cause, so they cannot serve as genuine supports for the same recurring process failure. Thus two supported failures with one common trace-level cause do not exist, and no permissible, source-grounded procedure remains that does not either invert indication/absence polarity or invent a drug-preference rule. Per the contract, I return null rather than inventing a medical rule or broadening the trigger. No trigger_terms are proposed because the condition (conditional_question) is already observed in T0026; the failure is not a detector miss but an unsupported-preference reasoning error that the contract bars me from encoding.

The required single trigger is pregnancy_context. Only two failures are in the allowed pool: T0082 and T0061. T0082 is the root case; its trace-level cause is the model treating absence of a pregnancy-category span as evidence against an otherwise-indicated option, while requiring positive pregnancy-category support (an absence-as-exclusion / span-as-preference error). However, encoding a procedure that fixes this would require asserting that one UTI agent is preferable over another in pregnancy at a given gestational age — a medical rule unsupported by the supplied labels (TMP-SMX label unavailable; no source ranks the agents). The contract forbids turning absence/presence of a label span into an option preference and forbids inventing a medical rule. T0061 is a dose-adequacy / next-step-in-management question about anti-D immune globulin quantification after fetal-maternal hemorrhage; its traced cause is entirely different (no indication/contraindication-span reasoning, no otherwise-indicated-option exclusion). Therefore T0082 and T0061 do NOT share one recurring trace-level cause, so two supported failures with a common process failure do not exist. Note also that T0082's observed_features list (dose_question, age_context, short_drug_options) does not even include pregnancy_context, so routing on pregnancy_context would need trigger_terms; but even after a detector-miss repair, the second required failure (T0061) still shares no common cause. Among the successes (T0020, T0078, T0041, T0018, T0086, T0034, T0060) several lie inside pregnancy_context, but they cannot anchor a card whose supporting failures do not form a single recurring cause. Any permissible procedure would either invert indication/contraindication polarity, convert span-absence into exclusion/preference, or state an unsupported drug-ranking rule. Per the contract I return null rather than inventing a medical rule or broadening beyond the two allowed failures. No trigger_terms are proposed because the blocker is not merely a detector miss but the absence of a second failure sharing the same trace-level cause.
